text: A day on Venus (one full rotation) lasts about 243 Earth days, longer than its year of about 225 Earth days.
Sunlight takes roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The Moon drifts away from Earth by about 3.8 centimetres every year.
Saturn has the lowest mean density of any planet, 687 kg/m³, less than water’s 1,000. Given a big enough bathtub, it would float.
A teaspoon of neutron-star material would weigh billions of tonnes.
Octopuses have three hearts.
Botanically, bananas are berries, while strawberries are not.
Crows can recognise individual human faces and remember them.
The human brain contains roughly 86 billion neurons.
Tardigrades have survived exposure to the vacuum of space in experiments.
Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings.
Hummingbirds are the only birds able to fly backward in a sustained way.
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
Sharks are older than trees: sharks date back over 400 million years, trees about 380 million.
Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth, because deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat.
Measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea is taller than Everest, at over 10,000 metres.
Russia spans 11 time zones.
Lightning can reach around 30,000 kelvin, several times hotter than the Sun’s surface.
The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from space. That is a myth.
Absolute zero is −273.15 °C, the lowest possible temperature.
Sound travels at about 343 metres per second in air at 20 °C.
Water is unusual: it expands as it freezes, which is why ice floats.
Euclid proved over 2,000 years ago that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
Euler’s identity, e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, links five of mathematics’ most fundamental constants.
Pi is transcendental, proved by Ferdinand von Lindemann in 1882, which settled that squaring the circle is impossible.
Brahmagupta wrote down rules for arithmetic with zero in 628 CE.
The number of possible chess games (Shannon’s estimate: about 10^120) dwarfs the roughly 10^80 atoms in the observable universe.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
The University of Oxford was teaching by 1096, centuries before the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325.
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 27 August 1896 is the shortest recorded war, lasting between 38 and 45 minutes according to differing reports.
Norse explorers had settled briefly at L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland around the year 1000.
Champollion deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822, using the Rosetta Stone.
Gutenberg’s movable-type printing press appeared in Europe around 1450.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.
Stretched out, the DNA in a single human cell would be about two metres long.
Saturn has more confirmed moons than any other planet: 274 as of March 2025.
Venus spins backward, so the Sun rises in the west there, and the time from sunrise to sunset is about 58 Earth days.
Voyager 1, launched in 1977, crossed the heliopause on 25 August 2012 and is now more than 25 billion kilometres from Earth.
Voyager 1 transmits with about 23 watts, roughly a refrigerator bulb, and its data reaches Earth at about 160 bits per second.
On its current path, Voyager 1 will pass within about 1.7 light years of the star AC+79 3888 in the year 40,272.
Sharks trace their origins back about 455 million years.
Cultivated bananas set fruit without pollination and are sterile, which is why they have no real seeds. They were domesticated around 7,000 years ago in Southeast Asia.
The Cavendish banana is roughly half of global banana production, and it faces the TR4 fungus.

Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the solar system: about 21.2 km above Martian zero elevation, or roughly 25 to 27 km above its own base. The figures differ because they use different reference points.
Olympus Mons is a shield volcano more than twenty times wider than it is tall, with an average flank slope of only about 4 degrees.

Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench, is the deepest known point in the oceans at about 10,900 metres, more than three times the average ocean depth of 3,682 metres. Published surveys differ by a few tens of metres.
The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second. It is not a measurement but a definition: since 1983 the metre itself has been defined from it.

Ancient Roman concrete, used in structures like the Pantheon, has proven remarkably durable, in part because lime clasts and reactions with seawater form self-healing mineral phases (Al-tobermorite and phillipsite) that reinforce the material over centuries.
The Pony Express, icon of the American West, operated for only 18 months (1860-1861) before the transcontinental telegraph made it obsolete.
The mantis shrimp can punch with the acceleration of a .22 caliber bullet, creating cavitation bubbles that reach 4,700°C—nearly as hot as the sun’s surface.
The wood frog can survive being frozen solid during winter, with up to 70% of its body water turning to ice, then thaw and resume normal activity.
Wombat feces are cube-shaped, with researchers confirming this results from the unique elasticity of their intestines, not diet—helping mark territory without rolling away.
LCD displays work by twisting liquid crystal molecules with electric fields; without power, some LCDs appear white while others appear black.
There are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth’s beaches—estimated at 10^24 stars versus roughly 10^18 to 10^19 grains.
The footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the Moon will likely remain visible for millions of years because there is no wind or water to erase them.
The largest known structure in the universe is the Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall, a galactic filament spanning roughly 10 billion light-years.
Saturn’s moon Titan has lakes and rivers of liquid methane and ethane, making it the only body in our solar system besides Earth with stable surface liquids.
The Pirahã people of the Amazon have no words for specific numbers, colors, or perfect tenses, and their language contains no recursion—challenging Chomsky’s theory of universal grammar.
The Basque language is a language isolate unrelated to any other known language on Earth, predating the arrival of Indo-European languages in Europe by thousands of years.
Africa is the only continent that spans all four hemispheres (Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western), extending from 37°N to 35°S and from 17°W to 51°E.
Russia has 11 time zones, but France holds the world record with 12 due to its overseas territories spanning from French Guiana to French Polynesia.

A pizza can be cut into 11 equal pieces using only 4 straight cuts, and more generally, n straight cuts can divide a circle into up to (n²+n+2)/2 pieces—far more than the 2n pieces most people expect.

The number 73 is the 21st prime number, and its reverse 37 is the 12th prime, while 21 is the product of 7 and 3—making it a 'prime factor mirror prime' and Sheldon Cooper’s favorite number in The Big Bang Theory.
Ancient Egyptians grew flax as an industrial crop.
Ancient Egyptian coffins were believed to act as a portal between the worlds of the living and the dead.
Ovis longipes palaeoaegyptiacus was one of the two most commonly domesticated sheep depicted on the reliefs of early pharaonic tombs.
era: Ancient Egypt (early pharaonic period, c. 3100-2686 BCE)

text: Ovis longipes palaeoaegyptiacus had unique, loosely spiraling horns that came out of the sides of the skull.

Before the marine chronometer, ships could determine latitude from celestial observations but had no reliable way to determine longitude at sea, because no timekeeper survived shipboard conditions accurately enough.

Quantum calculus (q-calculus) is sometimes called 'calculus without limits' because it develops derivatives, integrals, and analogous results without using the notion of limits, in contrast to traditional infinitesimal calculus.
The two types of calculus within quantum calculus are q-calculus and h-calculus.
In h-calculus, the original mathematical object is recovered by taking the limit as the parameter h tends to 0 of the h-analog.
Early astronomical records from the Babylonians date back to around 1000 BC.
Central American cultures showed astronomical interest in early history.
French scientists traveled to Campbell Island to observe the 1874 transit of Venus.
Multiple countries sent scientific expeditions around the world to observe the 1874 transit of Venus.
On December 8, 1874, British scientists conducted an astronomical expedition to observe the transit of Venus from three separate sites in the Hawaiian Islands.
The 1874 transit of Venus expeditions were designed to obtain an accurate estimate of the astronomical unit (AU), the distance from Earth to the Sun, by measuring solar parallax.
Scientists attempted to measure the astronomical unit by observing the transit of Venus in 1769.
The black drop effect hampered efforts to obtain a precise value of the astronomical unit during the 1769 transit of Venus observations.
The Cambridge Digital Library holds a collection of papers relating to the 1874 Transit of Venus Expedition to Hawaii.
Andean dark constellations are called 'yana phuyu' in Quechua, which literally translates to 'black cloud'.
Pre-Columbian civilizations of the Andes region identified astronomical configurations based on dark silhouettes rather than bright stars.
Andean dark constellations are formed by molecular clouds and interstellar dust lanes located along the Milky Way.
Abo Elementary School was designed to function as an advanced fallout shelter.
Abo Elementary School had a concrete slab roof that doubled as the school’s playground.
The American Committee for East–West Accord’s stated goals included promoting conciliation between the United States and the Soviet Union.
ADRON-RM is a neutron spectrometer designed to search for subsurface water ice and hydrated minerals.
The Alais meteorite contains organic compounds.
ANNIE studies phenomena like proton decay and neutrino oscillations by analyzing neutrino interactions in gadolinium-loaded water and measuring their neutron yield.
Neutron tagging plays an important role in background rejection from atmospheric neutrinos in the ANNIE experiment.
The Antiproton Decelerator was built from the Antiproton Collector (AC).
Antiprotons at CERN’s Antiproton Decelerator are created by impinging a proton beam from the Proton Synchrotron on an iridium target.
Aspect’s experiment offered an experimental answer to the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) paradox.
Tube Alloys was initiated during World War II.
Canada was involved in the Manhattan Project.
The United States initiated the Manhattan Project in 1942 in collaboration with the United Kingdom.
Israel is believed to have acquired nuclear weapons around 1967 but has never openly tested or formally acknowledged possessing them.
The five recognized nuclear-weapons states under the NPT are also the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.
The Classis Pontica coordinated with the neighboring Roman fleet of Moesia, known as the Classis Flavia Moesica.
Within the Mathematics Subject Classification, subsection 01A67 is titled 'Future prospectives'.
The Archimedes Palimpsest is a medieval parchment manuscript that was scraped and overwritten but originally contained several previously unknown works by Archimedes.
The Archimedes Palimpsest is a medieval manuscript that was found to contain erased and overwritten works of the ancient Greek mathematician Archimedes.
The Lwów School of Mathematics was a group of mathematicians who worked in the city of Lwów (present-day Lviv, Ukraine) during the interwar period.
The Scottish Café was a café in Lwów where mathematicians of the Lwów School of Mathematics recorded problems in a notebook known as the Scottish Book.
In the rhetorical stage of mathematical notation, calculations were described purely using words rather than symbols.
In the syncopated stage of mathematical notation, quantities and common algebraic operations began to be represented by symbolic abbreviations.
One modern hypothesis links Venus’s ashen light to lightning activity on the planet.
There is some evidence of lightning occurring on Venus.
The transient aurorae/airglow hypothesis attributes ashen light to unusually high solar activity interacting with the upper Venusian atmosphere.
Reported ball lightning sizes vary from pea-sized to several meters in diameter.
Ball lightning is reported to last considerably longer than the split-second flash of a lightning bolt.
A plate of peeled bananas has appeared on a street corner in Beeston, Nottinghamshire, every month for over a year, as of January 2025.
Until March 2025, the mysterious plate of bananas in Beeston appeared at the junction of Abbey Road and Wensor Avenue.
St. John’s, the provincial capital of Newfoundland and Labrador, is less than 20 kilometres (12 mi) east of Bell Island.
Georges Cuvier demonstrated evidence for the concept of extinction in 1796.
The French word 'paléontologie' was introduced in 1822.
Cenograms are used in studying ancient communities to draw conclusions about a biome, including whether it is species rich, its relative humidity, and its level of forestation.
Cenograms have become common in the study of prehistoric fauna of the northern hemisphere.
A majority of the 60 to 75 million people who died in World War II were civilians.
The Axis powers were later called the Rome–Berlin–Tokyo Axis.
One hypothesis for fairy circle formation proposes that the activities of various types of termites affect vegetation growth.
Another hypothesis for fairy circle formation proposes that competition between grasses naturally yields certain vegetation patterns.
Alyoshenka, also known as the Kyshtym Dwarf, is an infant whose mummified remains were discovered in the village of Kaolinovy, near Kyshtym, Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia.
Edgar Beecher Bronson, a big-game hunter, recounted the 1907 dingonek sighting in his 1910 memoir 'In Closed Territory'.
Above-threshold ionization (ATI) is a multi-photon effect in which an atom is ionized by absorbing more than the minimum number of photons energetically required for ionization.
The first observation of above-threshold ionization was made using xenon gas.

The Aharonov–Bohm effect is a quantum-mechanical phenomenon in which an electrically charged particle is affected by an electromagnetic potential despite being confined to a region where both the magnetic field and electric field are zero.
The Aharonov–Bohm effect is illustrated experimentally through interference experiments.
The Christmas Eve truce of 1944, also known as Truce in the Forest, was an informal ceasefire between American and German soldiers during World War II.
Fritz Vincken reportedly witnessed the Christmas Eve truce of 1944 as a child.
Fritz Vincken reportedly witnessed the truce in a remote cabin near the German–Belgian border.
Primordial gravitational waves are predicted by 'slow roll' models of cosmic inflation.
Ancient Egypt’s documented history spans approximately three millennia.
The current field of conservation paleobiology was established by the work of K.W. Flessa and G.P. Dietl during the first decade of the 21st century.
Dental microwear analysis has been used to investigate weaning practices in past human populations.
Evidence suggests that life on Earth emerged prior to 3.7 billion years ago.
The interpreting of aerial photographic images became an important new specialty during World War I, essential for accurate mapping.
By 1915, air-to-ground radio was in use by reconnaissance pilots during World War I.
New electronic forms of reconnaissance emerged as a sub-type of aerial reconnaissance during World War II.
In April 1989, Eric M. Jones and Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison H. Schmitt spent three days thoroughly reviewing part of Apollo 17’s lunar activities.
The Apollo Lunar Surface Journal contains corrected, annotated transcripts of all recorded conversations between astronauts on the lunar surface and mission control in Houston.
Harrison H. Schmitt introduced Eric M. Jones to the other 11 Apollo astronauts who had walked on the Moon, leading them to participate in recorded mission-review sessions.
The Apollo Lunar Surface Journal includes commentary from ten of the twelve astronauts who walked on the Moon.
Eric Jones received a NASA Distinguished Public Service Medal in 2023 for his work documenting Apollo history.
Apollo 8 was the first successful crewed mission to orbit the moon and return to Earth.
At the lunar south pole, nighttime can last for 14 Earth days.
NASA has targeted developing a 100-kilowatt nuclear reactor for use on the lunar surface.
Each Lunar Orbiter carried two cameras—one high-resolution and one medium-resolution—and used 70-millimeter film rather than standard 35-millimeter film.
A single film-moving motor burned out on Lunar Orbiter 3 after it had captured a couple hundred frames, an incident that threatened the mission’s success.
The word 'Pacific' derives from a version of 'pacify' or 'peaceful.'
About 94 percent of the plastics in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch are microplastics smaller than a grain of rice.
Ferdinand Magellan named the Pacific Ocean in 1520 after sailing through a calm patch of water, deriving the name from 'pacify' or 'peaceful.'
According to NOAA, ocean pH has fallen by 0.1 units over the past 200 years, making ocean waters 30 percent more acidic.
Chelle Gentemann compared the Pacific Blob with sea-surface-temperature records dating back to 1910 and found its magnitude and duration were unprecedented in that historical record.
A toxic algal bloom stretched along the entire West Coast of the United States during the Pacific Blob period.
The Pacific 'Blob' marine heatwave coincided with unexpected die-offs of California sea lions, Guadalupe fur seals, common murres, and Cassin’s auklets.
region: North Pacific / West Coast North America

text: The toxic algal bloom during the Pacific 'Blob' period delayed and partially closed recreational and commercial fishing seasons for sardines, anchovies, crabs, and razor clams.
region: US West Coast (California to British Columbia)

text: The AMOC has been continually monitored in one form or another only since 2004.
Temperature data for the sea just south of Greenland dates back to 1870.
Apollo 11 landed 4.2 miles from its intended target, the farthest off-target landing of the Apollo lunar missions.
In the Apollo lunar module, having astronauts stand rather than sit provided a 20-times-greater field of view from one-tenth the window area.

Apollo 7’s crew—Wally Schirra, Donn Eisele, and Walt Cunningham—reentered Earth’s atmosphere without wearing helmets, despite Mission Control’s warnings about cabin leaks, rapid depressurization, and landing impacts.
Apollo 7’s Service Propulsion System engine, rated at 20,500 pounds of thrust, fired eight times as planned during the mission.

Apollo 7 made the first live television broadcast from an American spacecraft, during which the crew displayed hand-lettered cue cards reading 'From the Apollo Room, High Atop Everything' and 'Keep Those Cards and Letters Coming In, Folks.'
Apollo 7 splashed down on October 22, 1968, 200 nautical miles south of Bermuda and only one mile from its aim point.
Rocketdyne supplied 33 engines for each Saturn V rocket, providing engines for every stage except the lunar module’s descent engine.

George Mueller’s 'all-up' testing philosophy meant the Saturn V’s first flight used all three live stages and a live Apollo command and service module, rather than testing stages incrementally with ballast.
The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), an ocean-current system that helps keep Europe warm, is currently the weakest it has been in more than 1,600 years.
A separate study using climate models and a century of ocean surface-temperature data concluded that AMOC weakening began in the mid-20th century and resulted from human-induced climate warming.
The deep Atlantic contains some of the world’s oldest and most spectacular cold-water coral reefs and deep-sea sponge grounds, which depend on ocean currents to deliver food and disperse offspring.
The La Niña following the unusually strong 1997/98 El Niño lasted 33 months and spanned three winters.
The Younger Dryas cold period began in less than 100 years and lasted roughly 1,300 years, occurring approximately 12,900 to 11,600 years ago.
region: global (most pronounced in North Atlantic region)

text: The warming that ended the Younger Dryas took only about 40–50 years, with Greenland ice-core samples showing temperature increases of up to 10°C (18°F) in just a few decades.
During the Younger Dryas, forests were replaced by tundra vegetation even though many parts of the tropics and Southern Hemisphere became warmer and wetter.
The Younger Dryas event occurred from 12,900 to 11,600 years ago and produced estimated cooling of 4–8 °C (7.2–14.4 °F) in northern Europe and eastern North America.
region: Northern Europe and Eastern North America (North Atlantic region)

text: The termination of the Younger Dryas cooling event occurred within a decade.
During the Younger Dryas, an abrupt shutdown of thermohaline circulation in the North Atlantic was associated with an influx of large volumes of freshwater from melting glaciers.
The Dansgaard-Oeschger cycles of the last glacial period represent alternation between two climate states, with rapid transitions from one state to the other.
At some GRIP/GISP2 sites near the summit of Greenland, annual snow and ice layers can be traced back more than 40,000 years, similar to counting tree rings.
Göbekli Tepe in southeastern Turkey contains T-shaped limestone megaliths, some exceeding 16 feet (5 metres) in height and weighing up to 50 tons.
Some megaliths at Göbekli Tepe are carved with elaborate images of foxes, scorpions, lions, and other animals.
Göbekli Tepe predates Stonehenge by approximately 6,000 years and is estimated to date to the 9th–10th millennium BCE.
Göbekli Tepe was first investigated in the 1960s but was dismissed at that time as a medieval cemetery, before being re-explored in the 1990s when its much greater age was recognized.
To test radiocarbon dating, Willard Libby borrowed objects with verified ages from museums, including a sandal found in an Oregon cave.

Soil samples from Abu Hureyra contained melt glass—vaporized soil that rapidly solidified—found alongside seeds, cereal grains, and splattered throughout adobe buildings, with most fragments measuring 1–2 millimeters across.
Abu Hureyra’s melt glass contained molten quartz, chromferide, and magnetite grains, minerals that melt only at temperatures between 1,720°C and 2,200°C.
Lightning was ruled out as the source of Abu Hureyra’s melt glass because lightning produces magnetic imprints that were absent from the samples.
Only 3 of the 29 archaeological sites re-examined by David Meltzer’s team had dates falling within the onset of the Younger Dryas.
era: modern (2014 study, referencing Younger Dryas ~12,900 years ago)

text: Experts initially studied Göbekli Tepe in the 1960s but dismissed it as a medieval cemetery; German archaeologist Klaus Schmidt revealed the complex’s true age in 1994.
Surveys indicate that about 15 additional rings of huge stones may remain buried beneath Göbekli Tepe’s soil.
A computer algorithm based on standard-deviation mapping found that three of Göbekli Tepe’s circular enclosures appear to form a geometric triangle.
The center points of three circular enclosures at Göbekli Tepe form a near-perfect triangle whose sides each measure approximately 63 feet.

Ground-penetrating radar and geomagnetic surveys at Göbekli Tepe mapped at least 16 additional buried megalith rings across 22 acres, while the excavated area covers only about one acre, less than 5 percent of the site.
University of Chicago and Istanbul University researchers examined Göbekli Tepe in the 1960s but dismissed the hill as an abandoned medieval cemetery after finding broken limestone slabs.

Since 1998, archaeozoologist Joris Peters of Ludwig Maximilian University in Munich has examined more than 100,000 bone fragments from Göbekli Tepe, of which gazelle bones account for more than 60 percent of the total.
era: Neolithic (c. 9600–8200 BCE excavation site; research since 1998)

text: Retired surgeon Derek Fawcett discovered a roughly three-foot-long wood fragment while digging a workshop foundation on his property in West Berkshire, 50 miles west of London.

The Nottingham Tree-ring Dating Laboratory and the University of Groningen’s Center for Isotope Research dated the West Berkshire wood artifact to between 4640 and 4605 B.C.E., with 95 percent confidence.
A wooden post unearthed in south Wales in 2012 had previously been considered the oldest wood carving found in Britain.
Researchers detected carbon spherules in soil layers from before, during, and after the Younger Dryas, not only at the event’s onset.
Most carbon spherules once attributed to a cosmic impact closely resemble tightly packed balls of fungus found in modern soils exposed to low-to-moderate heat during wildfires.
A scientific study on carbon spherules concluded the particles were of natural biological origin and unrelated to intense wildfires or cosmic impacts.
According to researcher Felisa Smith of the University of New Mexico, 80–90% of large herbivores' methane emissions are released through burps rather than flatulence.

A study estimated that the extinction of Ice Age megafauna removed just under 10 teragrams (about 10 million tons) of methane emissions, accounting for at least 12–15% (and possibly up to 100%) of the methane reduction at the start of the Younger Dryas.
Smaller versions of Göbekli Tepe’s pillars, symbols, and architecture have been found in settlements up to 125 miles away.
The Jebel Sahaba cemetery in northern Sudan is approximately 13,000 years old.
New technology detected dozens of additional wounds on the Jebel Sahaba skeletons beyond the arrowhead impact marks previously identified.
Göbekli Tepe’s largest enclosure, Building D, measures at least 65 feet across and contains two freestanding limestone pillars each 18 feet tall and weighing an estimated 8 tons.
Göbekli Tepe covers 25 acres and contains at least seven stone circles.
Göbekli Tepe’s stone circles range from 30 to 100 feet in diameter and are enclosed by rectangular stone walls about 6 feet high.

Archaeologist Klaus Schmidt and colleagues estimated that at least 500 people were needed to quarry, transport, and erect Göbekli Tepe’s 10- to 50-ton stone pillars, some moved from locations as far as a quarter-mile away.
Rapamycin extended lifespan in both male and female UM-HET3 mice, with females showing a greater benefit than males (Harrison et al., 2009; Miller et al., 2011, 2014).
Nordihydroguaiaretic acid (NDGA) failed to extend lifespan in female mice even at doses producing blood levels similar to those in males, and extended lifespan only in males (Harrison et al., 2014).
In 2023, 59.5% of US young adults aged 18–34 years (about 43.7 million people) reported at least 1 of 12 selected chronic conditions.
Taking 12,000 steps per day was associated with a 65% lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with taking 4,000 steps per day.
After accounting for total daily step count, researchers found no association between stepping intensity and risk of death.
In the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Study, lifestyle intervention was associated with a lower incidence of microvascular complications (hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.45–0.95; p=0.025).
In the Da Qing Diabetes Prevention Study, participants receiving lifestyle intervention had an average increase in life expectancy of 1.44 years (95% CI 0.20–2.68; p=0.023).

A single drug-use screening question about past-year illegal drug use or nonmedical prescription medication use was found to be 100% sensitive and 73.5% specific for detecting a drug use disorder in a primary-care setting.
In mice with natural aging equivalent to about 80 human years, an oral mixture of senolytic drugs extended lifespan by 36% compared to the norm for that type of mouse.
Older mice developed frailty and reduced survival from fewer transplanted senescent cells than younger mice did.

According to Halena Gazelka, M.D., the COVID-19 pandemic indirectly caused a significant increase in opioid overdoses in the United States, primarily due to illicit-market drugs such as fentanyl rather than clinical overprescribing.
The immortal jellyfish, Turritopsis dohrnii, can revert from adulthood back to its polyp stage when threatened by danger or starvation.
In a small (n=9) phase I open-label clinical trial, a 3-day oral course of dasatinib plus quercetin reduced senescent-cell markers in adipose tissue and skin of people with diabetic kidney disease.
A food product labeled '0 g trans fat' may still legally contain up to 0.5 grams of trans fat per serving.
The original rotavirus vaccine was withdrawn from the market by its manufacturer, Wyeth Ayerst Laboratories, after only one year.

A mathematical model published in npj Aging estimated that if nearly every reversible hallmark of aging were eliminated, leaving only somatic mutations, the median human life span would be 146–194 years.
In aging simulations, liver function often remained intact for tens of thousands of years because liver cells can regenerate.
During fasting, human growth hormone (HGH) levels increase in the body.
Short-term fasting may temporarily increase metabolic rate by increasing the release of norepinephrine, a fat-burning hormone.

About 90% of newborns infected with hepatitis B perinatally develop chronic infection, and one in four of those infected will die prematurely from liver disease, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Under CDC’s updated 2024 COVID-19 guidance, people may resume regular activities within 24 hours if they have been fever-free for at least 24 hours without medication and their symptoms are mild and improving.

On February 19, 2025, HHS issued guidance stating that the U.S. government would recognize only two sexes—male and female—defining sex as a person’s 'immutable biological classification' as either male or female.

HHS defines 'female' as a person with a reproductive system whose biological function is producing eggs, and 'male' as a person with a reproductive system whose biological function is producing sperm.
Only 39 of the 100 psychology studies examined in the Reproducibility Project were successfully replicated.
A survey identified data leakage in 22 papers across 17 research fields, collectively affecting 294 papers.

A study criticized for data leakage used anti-hypertensive-drug use as a feature to predict hypertension, even though that information would not be available when predicting the outcome for a new patient.
The Open Science Collaboration, a consortium of 270 scientists, attempted to replicate 100 published psychology studies and found that more than half of the replications failed.

Harvard researchers Daniel Gilbert, Gary King, and Stephen Pettigrew, along with University of Virginia professor Timothy Wilson, calculated that the number of failed replications in the OSC study was no greater than would be expected by chance, even if all 100 original findings were true.

A U.S. version of the affirmative-action replication study essentially reproduced the original result, but the Open Science Collaboration excluded this successful U.S. replication and included only the failed University of Amsterdam replication in its estimate of psychology’s reproducibility.
Researchers conducted a preregistered, high-powered direct replication of experiment 1 from the 2012 PNAS paper on signing location and honesty, and failed to replicate the original result.

In a study on interracial rejection, participants rejected by same-race partners showed greater cortisol increases immediately after the interaction than participants rejected by cross-race partners (F(1,86)=4.51, p=.037, d=0.46), though the difference became statistically nonsignificant 20 minutes later (F(1,86)=2.72, p=.10, d=0.36).
Researchers identified a previously unknown type of interneuron found only in primates, not in ferrets, mice, or other studied species.

The newly discovered primate-specific interneuron is located in the striatum, a brain structure associated with cognition, reward, coordinated movement, Huntington’s disease, and potentially schizophrenia.
The newly discovered interneuron accounts for approximately one-third of all interneurons in the primate striatum.
FCC measurements reported that even in major urban areas, only about 30% of allocated radio spectrum was being used at any one time.
In February 2002, the FCC allowed limited use of ultra-wideband (UWB) techniques in the 3.1–10-GHz spectrum.

UWB technology can spread a signal across gigahertz of spectrum while using only picowatts of power per hertz, causing the signal to appear as background radiation, or the noise floor, to conventional narrowband receivers.
Adding only a small fraction of ranking data to the training blend enabled instruction-tuned LLMs to outperform existing expert ranking models.
Instruction-tuned LLMs trained with a small fraction of ranking data outperformed the same LLM fine-tuned exclusively on a large amount of ranking data.
Llama3-RankRAG significantly outperformed Llama3-ChatQA-1.5 and GPT-4 models on nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks.
Without instruction fine-tuning on biomedical data, Llama3-RankRAG performed comparably to GPT-4 on five biomedical RAG benchmarks.
Ahmed et al. (2023) reported that private businesses' share of the biggest AI models increased from 11% in 2010 to 96% in 2021.

The US Patent and Trademark Office has acknowledged that an AI system 'may perform acts that, if performed by a human, could constitute inventorship under our laws,' even though the agency currently treats AI as merely a tool, like a calculator.
A European fertility group has called for an international cap on sperm-donor contributions after some donor-conceived people discovered they have hundreds of biological siblings.
Michael Marcus spent 25 years at the Federal Communications Commission, where he helped develop policies that made more than eight gigahertz of radio spectrum available for unlicensed use.
Google’s Gemma-2 9b and OpenAI’s GPT-4o achieved near-perfect scores on Anthropic’s DiscrimEval bias benchmark, released in December 2023.
AI melanoma-diagnosis systems perform better on white skin than black skin, largely because their training data contains more examples of white skin.
Google researchers achieved nearly 91% smile-detection accuracy on the Faces of the World (FotW) benchmark by training racial and gender classifiers as part of their model.
Google’s smile-detection model used a racial classifier trained on four race subgroups and a gender classifier with two categories.
Google researchers labeled gender categories in their smile-detection model as 'Gender 1' and 'Gender 2' specifically to reduce the risk of introducing unconscious societal bias.
The Supreme Court began audio recording oral arguments in 1955.

Juvenile representation is decreasing in all five G. agassizii recovery units, indicating inadequate recruitment across the entire recovery-unit system.

Leatherback sea turtle populations are declining in the Pacific Ocean but recovering in the Atlantic Ocean.

Nepal’s tiger population increased from 121 individuals in 2009 to an estimated 235 in 2018, nearly doubling in nine years.

Under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(E), Intelligence Community agencies are prohibited from disclosing records in response to FOIA requests made by any foreign government or international governmental organization, whether directly or through a representative.

Agencies have one year to respond to a Mandatory Declassification Review (MDR) request, compared with 20 working days for an initial FOIA response (with up to 10 additional working days allowed in unusual circumstances).
MDR requesters who disagree with an Interagency Security Classification Appeals Panel (ISCAP) decision have no further recourse and cannot pursue federal court litigation.

Under FOIA, an intelligence-community agency or component may not release records under the ordinary request provision to a foreign government entity other than a U.S. state, territory, commonwealth, or district, or to a representative of such foreign government entity.

Under the U.S. Freedom of Information Act, the deliberative process privilege does not apply to interagency or intra-agency memorandums or letters created 25 years or more before the date the records were requested.
Under FOIA, for qualifying noncommercial, educational, scientific, or news-media requests, agencies may not charge fees for the first two hours of search time or the first 100 pages of duplication.

Under FOIA, an agency must make electronic copies of records available when those records have been requested three or more times, or when their subject matter makes them likely to be the subject of similar future requests.
The FBI may treat the existence of classified records concerning foreign intelligence, counterintelligence, or international terrorism as exempt from FOIA disclosure requirements.
Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri was held briefly at the CIA’s 'Salt Pit' prison in Afghanistan before being transferred to a black site in Thailand.

After the Church Committee scandal, the FBI issued explicit guidelines intended to prevent abuses.
Under 49 U.S.C. § 114, the Under Secretary of Transportation for Security was appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, with a term of office of 5 years.

During a national emergency, the Under Secretary of Transportation for Security was authorized to coordinate domestic aviation, rail, surface, and maritime transportation, and to oversee transportation-related responsibilities of federal departments and agencies other than the Department of Defense and military departments.

The Under Secretary of Transportation for Security could issue an emergency regulation or security directive without notice, public comment, or prior approval from the Secretary of Transportation, and such a measure could remain effective for no more than 90 days unless ratified by the Transportation Security Oversight Board or rescinded.

A Transportation Security Administration employee or other federal employee designated as a law enforcement officer could carry a firearm, make a warrantless arrest for a felony based on probable cause, and seek and execute federal arrest or evidence-seizure warrants.

The Under Secretary of Transportation for Security could not take an aviation security action if the Federal Aviation Administration Administrator notified the Under Secretary that the action could adversely affect an aircraft’s airworthiness, unless the Secretary of Transportation subsequently approved the action.

The Secretary of Homeland Security was required to submit the initial National Strategy for Transportation Security and transportation modal security plans to Congress by April 1, 2005, and after December 31, 2005, submit updated versions at least once every even-numbered year.

The U.S. Census Bureau added "Mexican" as a racial category in 1930 for people born in Mexico or with Mexican-born parents who were "definitely not white, Negro, Indian, Chinese, or Japanese," but in 1936 the census director ordered that "Mexicans are Whites and must be classified as 'White.'"
A study found that when people from low- and high-income backgrounds live in the same neighborhood, more cross-class marriages form, but this pattern does not occur for interracial marriages.
Researchers Benjamin Goldman, Jamie Gracie, and Sonya Porter found that residential segregation does not explain the low rate of white-Black marriage in the United States.
A matching model calibrated on 2002–2007 CPS data explains much of the observed outward shift in the Beveridge curve between 2008 and 2013.

Employment and wage growth from 1980 to 2012 were especially strong in jobs requiring high levels of both math skill and social skills.
The Gulf of Mexico’s shallower waters at the impact site produced a dense cloud containing as much as 100 billion tons of vaporized sulfur.

The Open Science Collaboration’s article on psychological-science reproducibility was authored by a group of 270 coauthors.

In the UCSD sleep deprivation study, fMRI showed less activity in the prefrontal cortex during a sleep-deprived arithmetic task, a region associated with working-memory functioning.

Archaeologists found stone tools up to 3 million years old buried alongside fossils of Paranthropus in southwestern Kenya, providing evidence that a non-human hominin developed stone technology.
In 2010, scientists identified Denisovans, an archaic human lineage that went extinct around the same time as Neanderthals, using mitochondrial DNA extracted from a finger bone.

In 2022, researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory achieved nuclear-fusion net energy gain, and repeated the result in 2023, though the experimental apparatus consumed far more power than the fusion fuel produced.

Older female mice, equivalent in age to 60-year-old women, lived about 12 percent longer when given daily injections of the active ingredient in Ozempic compared to mice that did not receive the drug.
The Lagar Velho child’s grave was dug into a little-used section of a rock shelter, where pine branches were burned inside the pit before the body was placed there.
The Lagar Velho child’s skeleton also has a sloping chin region, evidence of well-developed arm musculature, and relatively short lower legs—features characteristic of Neanderthals.
The Lagar Velho burial included pierced deer teeth and shell ornaments, and the body was covered with red ochre pigment.
Archaeologists discovered an Indigenous settlement near Coatepec, Veracruz, dating back approximately 1,400 years.
The stone platform at the Coatepec, Veracruz settlement is nearly 100 feet long and 40 feet wide, decorated with lines, squarish shapes, and two circular stones.

The initial AI-assisted reading of a Vesuvius-burned scroll revealed 15 columns of text and more than 2,000 written characters about how to enjoy life, likely written by a follower of the Greek philosopher Epicurus.

Stonehenge’s altar stone originated in Scotland, hundreds of miles from Salisbury Plain, weighs more than six tons, and was transported approximately 4,600 years ago, probably without the use of wheels.

At least 20% of people who develop lung cancer are nonsmokers, according to Catherine Madaffari, M.D.

In a Mayo Clinic study, all 25 participants had two arthritic knees, and both knees improved dramatically even though only one knee received stem cells while the other received only a saline control injection.
Stomach size does not correlate with body weight; naturally thin people can have stomachs the same size as or larger than those of people who struggle with their weight.
The human small intestine is over 20 feet long, while the large intestine is about 5 feet long.

Comet 3I/ATLAS, discovered on July 1, 2025, is only the third known interstellar visitor to the solar system, following 1I/'Oumuamua in 2017 and 2I/Borisov in 2019.

A 2019 paper coauthored by Harvard’s Boaz Barak showed that double descent can occur not only as models gain parameters, but also when they receive more training data or are trained for longer.
